<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via create_upload_link (literal, a string literal in MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES), read_file (literal, a string literal in MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES))_
- `content/docs/ai/skills.mdx`  _(via SkillSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx`  _(via create_upload_link (literal, a string literal in MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via create_upload_link (literal, a string literal in MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES), read_file (literal, a string literal in MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via SkillSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via create_upload_link (literal, a string literal in MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES), read_file (literal, a string literal in MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ec05934df73e316d5df9f252c4dad7208c48dd12` — the merge of head `6c6b36bafd8bb1678cec427ffcd9a5159dffc99b` into base `1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ec05934df73e316d5df9f252c4dad7208c48dd12 && git checkout ec05934df73e316d5df9f252c4dad7208c48dd12
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df 6c6b36bafd8bb1678cec427ffcd9a5159dffc99b && git checkout -B drift-repro 1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df && git merge --no-ff 6c6b36bafd8bb1678cec427ffcd9a5159dffc99b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1282a464e9d27c2f8b86e69026087d1a1ff9b2df` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**L1 review · REWORK (paper only; the code is accepted as it stands)** · Head-sha: `239779897505af5d57ed02a9a3bcbc1a7d55d957` · card #34948 · read 2026-11-17T23:46Z

This is a full review: there is no earlier L1 record. I read the diff from merge-base `44430146` (2 commits, 9 files, +134 / -12), the card, the claim 6963114365 and dev report 6964304624.

**Route.** The card allows either route: list the tools in the registry, or have the rule resolve against the door's set, plus a test that holds the two equal. The PR takes the second route with that test. Keeping the pair out of `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE` holds up on two counts. `mcp-server-runtime.ts` sources its bridged `openWorldHint` from `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES`. The registry's header also promises that each group is exactly what one cloud package registers. The ui label-parity tests read that registry and nothing else, so no locale keys are owed.

**Code.**
- `collectToolUniverse` seeds the universe from both sets. Everything else that reads `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` reads it unchanged.
- `MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES` is `['create_upload_link', 'read_file']`. Those match the two `note(...)` registrations in `registerFileTools`, which returns `string[]`.
- **Pins.**
  - The mcp test checks that `registerFileTools(full bridge)` equals the constant and that the lint rule resolves each name. Its control: a bridge with no file member registers `[]`, so the equality is read from the registration sites.
  - The lint test resolves the pair, and its control `upload_file` is still reported at `skills[0].tools[2]`.
  - The spec tests require the list to be sorted, unique and snake_case, to share no name with the registry and to fall inside no family prefix.
  - The body reports an ablation (the constant dropped from the universe) that turned lint 1 and mcp 1 red. I did not re-run it.
- **Dependencies:** `@objectstack/mcp` already declares `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/spec`, and lint does not depend on mcp, so no new edge or cycle appears.
- **Generated artefacts:** the one new row in `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` is what a new export regenerates.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/lint` are both patch, which is the level `Metadata-protocol: none` takes. The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line fits: the rule now resolves two more names, and nothing that resolved before stops resolving.
- **Governance:** `check-governed-merges --pr 35034` says not governed, 146 lines.
- **Gates at this head (latest attempt per check):** none failed so far (18 success, 11 skipped, 36 still running).

### Should-fix (blocks; paper only)

- **S1: the surface extension is not recorded on the card.** The claim's File surface (6963114365) does not list `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, and the surface is stop-on-breach. The edit itself is right. `os explain ai-skill-tool-unresolved` lists the rule's sources, and the rule's own test pins that text, so adding a fourth source without it would publish a false sentence. The area has accepted the extension, but only in the area thread. A claim amendment comment on #34948 that adds `rule-explanations.ts` (as on #34791, 6959256004) puts the acceptance where the next reader and the land gate look. Once that is posted, I will turn this into a same-head ACCEPT with no further code reading.

### Nit

- **N1: the file pair is served over MCP only.** The rule's finding says an unresolved name is one "the runtime drops". After this change a skill bound to `read_file` is silent under `os lint`, but nothing in this repo shows the in-product chat runtime registering that name. The explanation's new clause says where the pair is served ("the file tools the MCP door registers"). It does not say that a chat turn may still go without them. A half-sentence there would keep the rule's promise exact. This is for the seat's contract review to weigh. It does not block.

**Owed, for the seat:** the contract review (Clause-② yes). Its face is the lint rule's resolution contract against the two runtimes, plus the new `@objectstack/spec/system` export. This comment readies, queues and arms nothing.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `239779897505af5d57ed02a9a3bcbc1a7d55d957`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts (the equality pin that enforces the constant's maintenance contract)

PR #35034, card #34948. Read: the card body and its 4 comments (triage 6956215495, claim 6963114365, dev report 6964304624, claim amendment 6964425901), the PR body and its 4 comments, the net diff from merge-base `4443014630` (9 files, +134 / -12), and the check-runs on this head. The rest of the diff (the two other test files, `api-surface/system.json`, `export-origins/system.json`, the changeset prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on this head, read 2026-11-17T23:5xZ: 0 failed. Green and relevant: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Build Core, Type Check source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, every Lint job, Test Core 7/10. Still running: Test Core 1-6 and 8-10, Type Check workspace, Type Check UI, Test UI 1-16. The spec, lint and mcp suites that hold this PR's three pins run in Test Core, so their CI verdict is not in yet; this record does not stand in for it.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: unchanged. `skill.tools[]` takes any string matching its regex before and after; no schema file is in the diff. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
- Public surface, spec: one new export, `MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES` (`readonly string[]`, two members) on `@objectstack/spec/system`. The one added row in each of `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` is what that export regenerates. Right.
- Public surface, lint: `ai-skill-tool-unresolved` resolves two more plain names. Side effects of seeding the universe, each right: a trailing wildcard whose prefix only these two names carry now resolves, and the near-miss suggestion can now offer the two names. Nothing that resolved before is reported now.
- `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE` and `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_TOOL_NAMES` are unchanged, and that is right for every reader I found in the live tree:
  - `worldAnnotation` in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts:529` asserts `openWorldHint: false` for registry members on bridged tools. The file pair is door-native, so membership would assert a hint with no source.
  - The ui chatbot label-parity tests and `ui/scripts/check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` read the registry for tools the in-product chat timeline shows. The chat does not run the pair, so no `chatbot.tool.*` label is owed.
  - `isPlatformProvidedToolName` keeps its meaning (registered by a cloud AI package).
  No reader of the registry should also see the file tools. The lint rule is the only one, and it reads the new constant.
- `os explain ai-skill-tool-unresolved` names the new source. Right as far as it goes; see S1 and N1.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — agreed. The diff adds one export and makes an advisory rule resolve two more names; it refuses nothing.

Changeset `.changeset/34948-mcp-file-tool-names.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/lint` patch. Both packages publish a change, and AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3) gives `patch` to `Metadata-protocol: none`, widening included. `@objectstack/mcp` changes a test only and publishes nothing, so it is rightly absent. Both declaration lines are in the PR body and the changeset body. Check Changeset is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` 1 (surface extension to `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`): answered A by claim amendment 6964425901. All 9 files lie inside the amended claim.
- `open_questions` 2 (does os-dev.md or the dispatch win when a consequence falls one file outside the listed surface): not answered on the card. It is a process ruling, not a property of this diff. Escalated to the seat; it does not gate this head.
- Out-of-scope finding a (seven other door tools still warn): filed as #35036 per the brief. Not re-raised.
- Out-of-scope finding b (`skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` says a name in none of three sources raises the rule): the report says noted, not filed. I found no card for it. It folds into S2.
- Dev's NOT MEASURED gate (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`): a CI gate after a full build. Build Core is green; the job that carries the gate is not identifiable from check-run names alone, so I read it as covered only once every check-run on this head is complete.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no off-relay write to name.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff has no data access, no id materialisation and no join.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-tool-names.ts` (hits).** The card allows either route; the PR takes "the rule resolves against the set the door registers, with a test holding the two equal". Placement holds: the constant sits beside the registry it is read with, the module header says why it is not a group, and `packages/spec` cannot import `packages/mcp`, so the conformance half has to live at the door, as the cloud groups' conformance lives in the cloud repo. The members match the live tree: `registerFileTools` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:3755`) has exactly two `server.registerTool` sites, `note('read_file')` and `note('create_upload_link')`, and returns the noted names. The name is exact for what it holds. The jsdoc's sentences each agree with the code.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-file-tools.test.ts` (the pin).** Real. It calls `registerFileTools` on a bridge carrying `readRecordFile`, `listRecordFiles` and `createUploadLink` with no scope filter, compares the returned names to the constant after sorting both, and its control (a bridge with no file member registers nothing) shows the equality is read from the registration sites. `@objectstack/mcp` already depends on `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/spec`; lint does not depend on mcp, so no cycle. The vitest alias reads lint from source.

**`packages/lint/src/validate-ai-tool-references.ts` (the rule).** The universe change is one line and does what the header says. Against the accepted scenario (hotcrm#2617: a receipts skill offered over MCP) it is right. It does not hold against the spec's own model of the field, which is where I could break it.

S1 (should-fix) — the rule now resolves the file pair for a skill that no MCP connection can ever be offered, so it is silent on a reference the skill's only runtime drops.
- `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts` says `tools` is bound by the cloud runtime and only read by MCP, where the binding decides whether the skill's prompt is offered. It also says `mcpPrompt: false` declares a skill written for the in-product agents only, never projected on any MCP connection whatever its binding, and that its `tools` "are validated as before".
- `projectSkillPrompt` (`packages/mcp/src/skill-prompts.ts:157`) returns null for `mcpPrompt: false`, and also for a skill with no `instructions`.
- The new constant's jsdoc states that no cloud AI package registers either name.
- So `{ name: 'receipts', mcpPrompt: false, tools: ['read_file'] }` passes `os lint --strict` at this head, while the cloud runtime (the only runtime that reads it) drops `read_file` without a word. That is the exact failure the rule's header and its explanation's last paragraph say it exists to catch, and before this PR the rule caught it.
- The fix is small and keeps the card's scenario: resolve `MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES` per skill, only where the skill is MCP-projectable (at least `mcpPrompt !== false`; the seat decides whether "has instructions" joins the condition), with a pin whose control is the same skill with `mcpPrompt: false` still reported. If the seat instead rules that the rule stays skill-blind, that ruling has to be written on the card and the limit stated in the explanation.

S2 (should-fix) — the resolution ladder is restated as an exhaustive three-source list in places the PR did not update, one of them the published spec jsdoc for the field itself. The dev applied the rule "a published text this change makes false is fixed in the same PR" to `rule-explanations.ts` only.
- `packages/spec/src/ai/skill.zod.ts:366-371`: "A name here resolves against, in order:" then three sources. Ships in the spec package as the field's contract.
- `packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts:1345-1347`: "a universe of three limbs".
- `packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts:691-693`: "`collectToolUniverse` unions" three sets. The reasoning these two comments carry (a per-write snapshot has no truthful unresolved verdict) still holds; only the enumeration is stale.
- `content/docs/ai/tools.mdx:193`: "resolves against three sources, in order".
- `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:85`: "A name in none of the three raises" the rule. Governed; the dev named it and left it unfiled.
Write these after S1, since S1 changes what the fourth source's sentence has to say. The spec jsdoc and the two lint comments belong in this PR. The docs page and the governed skill may go to one filed follow-up card that names both; without a card they are not closed.

N1 (nit, carried from L1 6964438978) — the explanation says where the pair is served ("the file tools the MCP door registers") but not that an in-product chat turn runs without them, while the rule's finding text still describes an unresolved name as one "the runtime drops". For a skill offered on both surfaces the rule cannot know which one the author means, so silence is the right verdict there; the half-sentence belongs in the explanation. S1's fix rewrites this sentence, so it is closed there at no extra cost.

N2 (nit) — the pin reads the door's set from `registerFileTools`' own `note(...)` bookkeeping. A future `server.registerTool` call in that function that skips `note` escapes this case, and the older case at `mcp-file-tools.test.ts:280` filters by a hand list, so it would not catch it either. Comparing against the server's listed tools would close it. Left as an accepted deviation or for #35036, which will touch the same pin.

N3 (nit) — #35036 will bring up to seven more door tools. A published export named for the file pair then either gains siblings or is subsumed by a wider door list; the second costs a deprecation. Nothing to change here; #35036 should decide the shape before it adds a second constant.

No must-fix. S1 and S2 are open on this head and owe a delta review of their fix.

Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**L1 delta review · REWORK (PR body only; the code is accepted)** · Head-sha: `71597ee0a5b374e520d3ee18cfd586fbce1d450e` · card #34948 · read 2026-11-18T00:48Z

This reviews the delta from L1 6964438978 (ACCEPT at `23977989`). The delta is one commit, `71597ee0` (8 files, +74 / -22), a fast-forward with no main merge. It answers the seat's contract review 6964565007 (S1, S2) under claim amendment 6964615710, which lists every path in it. Dev delta report 6965484702.

- **Seat S1 is closed, and with it my N1.** `collectToolUniverse` no longer holds the pair. `validateAiToolReferences` builds `shared` and `withMcpFileTools`, and picks one per skill through `offeredOverMcp(skill)`, which is `skill.mcpPrompt !== false` and nothing else, per the seat's ruling. `resolves` takes the universe as an argument, so the trailing-wildcard branch follows the same per-skill set. The control pin checks that `{ mcpPrompt: false, tools: ['read_file'] }` gives exactly one finding at `skills[0].tools[0]`, and that an absent key or `true` resolves. The `os explain` pin now requires "only for a skill offered over MCP" and `mcpPrompt: false`. The body reports that ablating `offeredOverMcp` to `return true` fails the control. I did not re-run it. The explanation, the constant's jsdoc and the changeset all state the limit. `mcpPrompt` is the existing `SkillSchema` key (`skill.zod.ts` 233, 352).
- **Seat S2 is closed.** The three restatements of the resolution ladder (`skill.zod.ts` tools jsdoc, `authoring-rules.ts`, `reference-integrity-suite.ts`) now name the fourth source and its condition. All three edits are jsdoc or comment text, with no `.describe()` and no schema change, so nothing generated moves. The two published restatements outside this PR (`content/docs/ai/tools.mdx`, `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`) go to the follow-up card named in the amendment.
- **Changeset:** still patch for both packages, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. The Clause-② widening now covers fewer cases than before, and nothing that resolved before the PR stops resolving.
- **Gates at this head (latest attempt per check):** 0 failed, 58 success, 11 skipped, 0 running.

### Should-fix (blocks; paper only)

- **S1: the PR body still describes the earlier behaviour.** "What changes", "Verification" and 维护者速读 say the rule resolves the pair for every skill. Since `71597ee0`, it resolves it only where `mcpPrompt !== false`, and a `mcpPrompt: false` skill naming the pair is still reported. The body is what the maintainer and the next reader land from, so it should state the condition and list the new control pin. This is a body edit only. Once it is done I will turn this into a same-head ACCEPT.

### Nit

- **N1: the #34167 pin's title is now false for the pair.** `validate-ai-tool-references.test.ts:60` says "checks the tools of a skill its owner keeps out of MCP (mcpPrompt: false) exactly as without the key". It still passes only because its fixture names no file tool. The new control covers the behaviour, so this does not block. A retitle that narrows it to the cloud-registry and action limbs ("… exactly as without the key, but for the MCP door's file tools (#34948)") would keep the test names true. If you fold it into this round, it is a one-line delta.

**Owed, for the seat:** the contract-review delta for `23977989..71597ee0`. This comment readies, queues and arms nothing.

This follows L1 6965528282 (REWORK, PR body only) at the same head. The code is unchanged.

- **S1 is closed.** The amended body states the condition (`mcpPrompt !== false`) in 维护者速读, What changes and Tests.
